newsitem.title: FRANCE: Interest rate fall cannot fail to help econ - Juppe.
newsitem.headline: Interest rate fall cannot fail to help econ - Juppe.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Tuesday interest rates had eased in a way France could only have dreamed of a year ago and could not fail to benefit the economy, companies and private individuals.
"I remember summer 1995 when short-term interest rates were above six points. We dreamed of an easing which would bring rates back to between four and 4.5 percent," Juppe said.
"You've seen the latest figures. We've fallen below 3.5 percent, around six percent for long term rates," he told the Senate.

"This exceptionally favourable move cannot but have an effect on the economy as a whole, to the benefit of local authorities, companies which invest and private individuals who are equipping houses or buying homes," he said.
The rates easing was "of a kind never seen", he said.
